title: System Health and Audit Reporting
card: Every automated action on the platform, graded and written in plain sentences.
what: A reporting layer I built to turn everything the platform did overnight into something a person can read in a minute.
problem: The platform grew one system at a time, and each system brought its own background services with it: syncs, watchers, nightly rebuilds. Dozens of them report in now, too many to check by hand each morning.
result: A digest lands every morning with last night's outcome for every service, including the ones that failed and recovered on their own. A page goes out only when a person has to act. A second machine watches the platform from outside and emails if it goes quiet, and the platform pages if that watcher dies.
how: Two kinds of record back it: what a service did and how many records it touched, and the field-level before and after of every change it made. The grading rules live in the reporting layer and not in the jobs themselves, so changing what counts as notable is one edit and never a re-run of anything.

Bug reports work the same way. Every page keeps a short rolling buffer of what happened in the browser, and none of it leaves the machine until someone clicks the feedback button and describes the problem, so a report arrives with the evidence already attached.

shot.alt: Service controls for the platform's background work. Each named service reports whether it is running and can be stopped from its own row: the tax sync, the deal drift monitor, the inventory and order heartbeats, the restock and email campaign syncs, the document store shipment sync, and the nightly full sync.
shot.caption: Each row names the outside system it depends on, and all of them report into the same morning digest.
